title: Use a Graphical User Interface (GUI)-based word processor to format documents

lessons.title: Formatting text
lessons.html:
Why we format documents

A word processor such as Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer or Google Docs lets you type documents and make them look neat. Formatting means changing how text and pages look. Good formatting makes a job card, service report, notice or letter easy to read.

Selecting text

Before you format, you must select (highlight) the text:

  • Double-click a word to select it.
  • Triple-click to select a whole paragraph.
  • Click and drag across text to select it.
  • Press Ctrl+A to select everything.

Font formatting

The font group on the Home tab has these tools:

ToolWhat it doesShortcut
Font typeChanges the style of letters, such as Arial or Calibri
Font sizeMakes letters bigger or smaller (for example 11 or 14)
BoldMakes text darker and thickerCtrl+B
ItalicSlants the textCtrl+I
UnderlineDraws a line under the textCtrl+U
Font colourChanges the colour of the text
HighlightPuts colour behind the text

Tips

  • Use one or two clear fonts in a document.
  • Use size 11 or 12 for normal text, bigger for headings.
  • Use bold for headings or important words such as WARNING.
  • Do not use too many colours. Dark text on a white page is easiest to read.

Copying formatting

The Format Painter (a paintbrush button) copies formatting from one piece of text to another. Select the formatted text, click Format Painter, then select the text you want to change.

lessons.title: Formatting paragraphs and lists
lessons.html:
Making paragraphs neat

Alignment

  • Left align: text lines up on the left. Best for most writing.
  • Centre: text is in the middle. Good for titles.
  • Right align: text lines up on the right. Sometimes used for dates.
  • Justify: text lines up on both sides.

Line and paragraph spacing

Line spacing is the space between lines. Use 1.0 or 1.15 for most documents. Paragraph spacing adds space before or after a paragraph so the page does not look crowded. Find these under Paragraph settings.

Indents and tabs

An indent moves a paragraph in from the margin. Use the Increase Indent button. Tabs line up text in columns. Press the Tab key rather than pressing the space bar many times, because spaces do not line up properly.

Bullets and numbering

Lists make information easy to read.

  • Use bullets for items in no special order, such as a list of tools needed.
  • Use numbering for steps that must be done in order, such as the steps to change engine oil on a tractor.

Select the lines and click the Bullets or Numbering button. Press Enter after an item to start the next one. Press Enter twice to end the list.

Example: service steps

  1. Park the tractor on level ground and switch off.
  2. Let the engine cool.
  3. Place a drip tray under the drain plug.
  4. Remove the plug and drain the oil.

Borders and shading

You can put a border around a paragraph or add shading, for example to make a safety warning stand out. Do not overuse this.

Styles

Styles such as Heading 1, Heading 2 and Normal apply a set of formatting at once. Using styles keeps all headings the same.

lessons.title: Page layout, tables and printing
lessons.html:
Setting up the page

Page layout options

  • Paper size: in South Africa we normally use A4.
  • Orientation: portrait (tall) for most documents, landscape (wide) for wide tables.
  • Margins: the white space around the edge. Normal margins are fine for most work.
  • Page break: starts a new page. Use Insert, Page Break instead of pressing Enter many times.

Headers, footers and page numbers

A header is at the top of every page; a footer is at the bottom. Put the company name or document title in the header and page numbers in the footer. Click Insert, then Header, Footer or Page Number.

Tables

Tables are good for lists with columns, such as a machine service record.

  1. Click Insert, then Table, and choose the number of columns and rows.
  2. Type in the cells. Press Tab to move to the next cell.
  3. Make the top row bold as headings.
  4. Change column widths by dragging the lines.
  5. Add a row by pressing Tab in the last cell.
MachineHoursService done
Tractor T051 250Oil and filters
Baler B02430Greasing

Pictures

You can insert a photo, such as a damaged part. Click Insert, Pictures, find the file. Drag a corner to resize so the picture does not stretch.

Checking and printing

  • Run spell check (F7 in many programs).
  • Read the document again to find mistakes spell check misses.
  • Use Print Preview to see what the page will look like.
  • Choose the printer, number of copies and pages, then print.
  • Save your work often with Ctrl+S.

Key points

  • Select text before you format it.
  • Use bold, size and clear fonts to make headings stand out.
  • Use numbering for steps in order and bullets for other lists.
  • Use page breaks, headers, footers and page numbers for neat pages.
  • Use tables for information in columns.
  • Spell check, read again and use print preview before printing.
